overview: LiquidSense Dev's Blink cancels the entire C03PacketPlayer family at the packet-event stage and keeps a selective replay queue: only the C04PacketPlayerPosition, C06PacketPlayerPosLook, C08, C0A, C0B and C02 subclasses are stored, while a bare C03PacketPlayer, the rotation-only variant, is cancelled and dropped permanently, which freezes the server-side yaw for the whole blink. Pulse mode is on by default: every pulseDelayValue milliseconds (default 1000, range 500 to 5000) a drain named blink() empties the LinkedBlockingQueue through the normal NetworkManager.sendPacket path behind a disableLogger flag so the re-entrant packet event does not re-capture the flushed packets. With pulse off a fakePlayer ghost (entity id minus 1337) is spawned at the enable position, and the render layer draws a breadcrumb line strip from recorded positions, colored by the Breadcrumbs module's palette.

sections.p: onPacket cancels every C03PacketPlayer instance, then the second branch re-cancels and stores only the position-bearing subclasses plus C08, C0A, C0B and C02. The plain C03, which carries yaw and pitch without a position, is cancelled without storage, so rotation updates vanish for the whole blink: the server-side player's head stays frozen while the body teleports forward on each pulse. The LinkedBlockingQueue preserves send order, which matters because a flushed C04 followed by its C06 must reach the server in the original sequence.

blink() sets disableLogger, drains the queue one packet at a time through mc.getNetHandler().getNetworkManager().sendPacket, and clears the flag in a finally-equivalent structure; the logger guard is what prevents the flushed packets from being re-cancelled by onPacket, since sendPacket fires the same PacketEvent. onUpdate polls MSTimer.hasTimePassed against pulseDelayValue and triggers a drain when the delay elapses, and onEnable resets the timer. The positions list, seeded with two points on enable, is appended every update tick and cleared on each drain, so the line strip shows the path since the last pulse.

The default 1000ms pulse means a burst of every buffered packet once per second, with each burst sized by how many packets accumulated in that second. The fakePlayer ghost and the line strip are cosmetic, and the dropped rotation packets mean the server sees a frozen yaw during the blink window, a detail a rotation-aware anticheat can correlate with the periodic teleports.

files.label: Blink.java
files.explanation: onPacket is the intercept: the whole C03PacketPlayer family is cancelled, the position-bearing subclasses and combat packets are queued for later replay, and bare C03s are dropped, freezing server-side rotation. blink() drains the LinkedBlockingQueue under the disableLogger guard, onUpdate pulses it via MSTimer, and the fakePlayer ghost is spawned only when pulse is off. onRender3D draws the position line strip using the Breadcrumbs module's color values.

files.label: MSTimer.java (pulse clock)
files.explanation: The pulse clock: hasTimePassed compares System.currentTimeMillis against a stored deadline, onEnable resets it, and onUpdate polls it every tick. The 1000ms default and 500ms minimum bound how often the drain fires, and that cadence directly sets the burst pattern the rate checks observe: one concentrated packet group per second, in a single tick, instead of a steady stream.

countering.label: MorePackets (per-second burst)
countering.explanation: NoCheatPlus MorePackets buckets moves into 500ms windows with a 22 per second ceiling and a 15-packet half-second burst path. The default 1000ms pulse drains roughly one second of movement in a single tick, so a player that moves continuously accumulates around 20 C03s per pulse, which trips the newest-bucket burst path on every cycle, and a faster player pushes the window accumulator above the ceiling as well. The 500ms minimum pulse delay makes the burst path the consistent hit, since even the fastest legitimate pulse concentrates a full second of packets.

countering.label: SurvivalFly (stale replay envelope)
countering.explanation: Each pulse replays a path that is stale by up to the pulse delay, so the first flushed move is the distance walked since the last drain. At sprint speed that is over five blocks, far beyond the per-move horizontal allowance SurvivalFly computes from the tracked location through prepareSpeedEstimation, so the first move of every pulse violates the envelope and earns a set-back. The pulse mode avoids the long silent gap but replaces it with a periodic teleport-sized first move, which the envelope sees on every cycle.

countering.label: MovingListener (set-back teleports)
countering.explanation: NoCheatPlus set-backs teleport the player to the recorded set-back location through SchedulerHelper.teleportEntity. With pulse on, a set-back that lands between drains leaves the next drain replaying a path that begins at the pre-correction position, so the envelope re-flags the divergence from the corrected location and set-backs again; each pulse re-triggers the correction that the previous pulse earned. The module never touches incoming S08 packets, so every correction applies and every replay pays for it.

countering.label: MorePackets (Arc v2 rate ceiling)
countering.explanation: Arc v2 MorePackets compares per-second counters of flying and position packets against the max-packets limit (default 30) and kicks when either exceeds max-packets-kick (default 70). The pulse drain concentrates a second of moves into one tick, so the counters climb by the whole pulse size at once; a player sending 30 or more C03s per second trips the ceiling on every pulse, and a fast player can cross the kick threshold outright. The check reads MovingData counters incremented by the moving listener, so the burst arrives as one large count rather than a distributed stream.
